question: Prove that there are infinitely many prime numbers.
Prove that the square root of 2 is irrational.
Prove that the sum of the first n odd numbers is n squared.
Prove that in any group of six people there are three who all know each other or three who are all strangers.
Prove that a graph is bipartite if and only if it has no cycle of odd length.
Prove that every tree with n vertices has exactly n - 1 edges.
Prove that the harmonic series 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + ... diverges.
Prove that the set of real numbers is uncountable.
Prove that for any integer n, n cubed minus n is divisible by 6.
Prove that the angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees in Euclidean geometry.
Prove that a continuous function on a closed interval attains a maximum.
Prove that the arithmetic mean of two non-negative numbers is at least their geometric mean.
Prove that if a prime p divides a product ab, then p divides a or p divides b.
Prove that the number of subsets of a set with n elements is 2 to the power n.
Prove that every positive integer greater than 1 can be written as a product of primes.
Derive the formula for the sum of a geometric series and state when the infinite series converges.
Prove that the halting problem is undecidable.
Show that comparison-based sorting needs at least on the order of n log n comparisons in the worst case.
Explain why the determinant of a matrix is zero exactly when its columns are linearly dependent, and prove one direction.
Prove that Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths when all edge weights are non-negative, and show why a negative edge breaks it.
Derive the escape velocity from the surface of a planet of mass M and radius R.
Explain from conservation of energy and momentum why a perfectly elastic head-on collision of equal masses swaps their velocities.
Prove that the eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix are real.
Prove that there is no largest even number.
Show that the expected number of coin flips to get the first head with a fair coin is 2.
